column3: NASB supplies “when”; “staying” renders “sojourning,” and “remote part” renders “remotest parts.”
“played the harlot against him” follows the Hebrew verb; the gloss here, “was angry,” reflects the Greek reading.
“speak tenderly to her” renders “speak to her heart.”
“detained him” renders “took hold of him.”
“Sustain yourself” renders “Sustain your heart.”
“let your heart be merry” renders “let your heart be good.”
NASB adds “again.”
“wait until afternoon” renders “delay until the day declines.”
“go home” renders “go to your tent.”
NASB puts “that is, Jerusalem” in parentheses.
“the day was almost gone” renders “the day had gone down greatly.”

“set on them” renders “went for them.”
“When they entered” renders “and he went.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“the traveler” renders “the man who was traveling.”
“going to my house” follows the Greek; the Hebrew reads “going to the house of the LORD.”
“your maidservant” renders “for your maidservant”; “bread” renders “food.”
“let me take care of all your needs” renders “all your lack is on me.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“making merry” renders “making their heart good”; “have relations with” renders “know.”
“my fellows” renders “my brothers”; “act of folly” renders “disgraceful folly.”
“ravish” renders “afflict”; “whatever you wish” renders “what is good in your eyes.”
“raped” renders “knew”; “at the approach of dawn” renders “as the dawn came up.”
“As the day began to dawn” renders “at the turning of the morning.”
“lying” renders “fallen.”
“home” renders “place.”
“limb by limb” renders “to her bones.”
“Consider it” renders “Set it to yourselves.”
